Seminar Title:

Analytical Model of Acoustic Scattering from Certain Rigid, Smooth, Star-Convex Bodies with Moderate Aspect Ratios

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Industrial Design

Speaker Name:

Nirlipta Pallabee Samapika ( Rollno : 519id1008)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Department Seminar Room

Date and Time:

15 May 2026 10 AM

Contact:

Dibya Prakash Jena

Abstract:

Acoustic scattering from underwater objects is used for detection, localization, tracking, etc., and has both military and civilian applications. Classical methods are used to analyse scattering from canonical forms such as infinitely long circular cylinders and spheres. Here, a new method is presented to analytically study scattering from certain infinitely long cylinders with more general cross-sections and axisymmetric bodies. The cross-sections of the bodies are single-valued functions of the angular coordinate in the cylindrical or spherical coordinate system, and, therefore, star-convex. The cross-sections are smooth as they have C1&nbspcontinuity. The aspect ratio, which is the ratio of the diameters of the smallest inscribing and circumscribing circles is moderate. Numerical results are shown for cylinders with cross-sections that are ellipses, compound ellipses which are egg-shaped, Cassini ovals, and for prolate and oblate spheroids and compared with those obtained using COMSOL&copy. Results are presented for objects with aspect ratio ranging from 0.47 to one and normalised frequency, ka, up to 15 where k&nbspis the acoustic wave number and a&nbspis a characteristic dimension of the cross-section.
